title: Annotatio II §.IV: Primary anti-absorption intent twisted into ante-usum hypostatic-style union
pass_a_gloss: All which places, primarily aimed lest it be believed that after the spiritual Union of Christ’s body with the bread in the Eucharist duly and rightly celebrated some abolition or absorption of the bread occurs — all who prepared themselves an entrance to Consubstantiation have borne to bend them thither, so that after consecration of the bread they imagined Christ’s Body united to it even before its use in no other way than that, after the mother of Christ blessed among women and greeted by the Angel, the divine person associated itself in a substantial mode with the human nature of Christ conceived in her womb and was united with it into one and the same ὑφιστάμενον.
pass_b_english: Those texts first meant to block belief that after spiritual bread–body union the bread is abolished or absorbed.
Consubstantiation-seekers bend them instead: after consecration, even before use, they imagine union like the divine person joining Christ’s human nature in Mary’s womb into one ὑφιστάμενον.
source_text: Quæ loca omnia, in id Primariò intenta, ne crederetur, post spiritualem corporis Christi, cum pane, in Eucharistia, ritè debitèque celebrata, Unionem, panis abolitionem quandam seu absorbitionem contingere, istuc flectere sustinuerunt quotquot ad Consubstantiationem sibi aditum pararunt, ut post consecrationem panis, cum hoc ipso, etiam ante usum ejus, Corpus Christi non alio modo uniri sibi imaginarentur, quàm, post benedictam inter mulieres ab Angelo salutatam matrem Christi, in hujus utero, conceptæ humanæ Christi naturæ divina persona, substantiali sese modo, sociavit cumque ista in unum idemque ὑφιστάμενον unita est.
notes: Anti-absorption bent to ante-usum hypostatic analogy.
